A correct pass needs the FULL served Mayhem/Vortex corpus (both this wave's batch and the prior 92-show wave) scanned systematically, in chronological order, not a partial view.

THOMAS AND PATRICK!"), finishing with a move called "Kissing the Blarney Stone II" (echoing Sean McClancy's own registered finisher, "Kissing the Balrney Stone III"). The UWF text bills their return explicitly as a comeback ("THE FORMORIANS ARE BACK") and has them appear in UWF Muscle Shirts. review_queue.name: GW's own pre-2002 name may have been GWF (Global Wrestling Federation) — found applying the GW handoff, not itself asked for
review_queue.note: Found while applying the GW accession handoff (lot 0040, 2026-08-23), verifying its §5 GWF non-conflation note before filing it — NOT itself one of the handoff's asks, and the handoff's own claim that "GWF (Global Wrestling Federation) is a separate ledger row explicitly distinguished from this GW on PTC's own site" appears to be backwards. PTC's own site carries two primary-source documents that read as GW's own former identity, not a distinct fed: (1) promotions/ptc/archive/gw-profile-2002.html, PTC's own "Member Profile: GW" page, verbatim: "Global Wrestling opening as two feds UCWF [Universal Championship Wrestling Federation] and FWL [Freedom Wrestling League]. Merged at a Joint PPV called Wrestle War. June 25, 2000. Bourn as GWF [Global Wrestling Federation] GW has come a long way and has gone though a lot of changes." — naming Bubba McCoy, Salaok, and Silent Wind as GW's own then-current champions, so this is unmistakably about the held GW, not a different fed. (2) promotions/ptc/archive/news-2002-04.html, a 14 April 2002 interview with "GW's Rookie Sensation Kwik FX": Alexis Steel asks "What is your take on the History of GW, and its transition from GWF to GW over this last month?"; KFX answers "there were so many checks I signed to the GWF's bill, that once it became GW I spent an hour erasing F's" — an explicit in-fiction rename, dated to roughly March 2002. If this holds up on a full read, GW's own founded/history fields (currently "No founding statement survives" and founded circa 2000 by indirect inference, data/promotions.json's gw row) understate what the record actually has: a stated founding date (25 June 2000, merger of a "UCWF [Universal Championship Wrestling Federation]" — a THIRD, distinct expansion of that acronym from the two already on data/frontier.json's own UCWF rows — and "FWL [Freedom Wrestling League]") and a named former identity (GWF, renamed to GW c. March 2002). None of this is applied here — it wants a full read of both documents and a deliberate integration into the GW promotion row, not a side-effect of a handoff pass — but it is filed so it isn't lost, and so the existing frontier.json "GWF" row (Adien Pryde's UWF bio + a fandom-wiki GWF founded 2006 — clearly a different, later fed, not this one) isn't mistakenly enriched with this GW material by a future pass moving too fast on the acronym alone. The handoff's own §5 GWF item is NOT applied as written (see this pass's own report) pending this.
review_queue.resolution_note: VERDICT (the Janitor, 2026-08-23: "Should GWF just be an aka?" — yes): CONFIRMED AND APPLIED. The fed renamed itself. Both documents this entry names were read in full and hold up: PTC's own "Member Profile: GW" dates the founding to a UCWF/FWL merger at a joint Wrestle War pay-per-view of 25 June 2000 and says the fed was "Bourn as GWF [Global Wrestling Federation]", on a page whose own "Quick GW facts" name Bubba McCoy's leadership and Salaok and Silent Wind among the then-current champions — unmistakably the held GW; and PTC's own newsdesk of 14 April 2002 carries Kwik FX on "its transition from GWF to GW over this last month," dating the change to roughly March 2002. Applied as data/promotions.json's gw row gaining aka: ["GWF", "Global Wrestling Federation"] under v77's new promotion-level aka[], plus a provenance_notes[] entry carrying both quotations. NOT applied, deliberately, and each left for a session that reads the documents it would touch: the stated 25 June 2000 founding (the row's own founded stays circa 2000 on its existing indirect receipt — a stated founding date is a real refinement and wants its own pass, not a side effect of this one), the UCWF and FWL merger parties, and the third distinct expansion of "UCWF" this profile introduces against data/frontier.json's own two UCWF rows. NOT MERGED, per the collision doctrine: the frontier's own 2006-founded "GWF" row is a different, later fed and now says so in its own note, and the separate unresolved "GWF (Global Wrestling Federation)" row off PCW's Recognition Lineup is left standing with a sentence recording the open question rather than folded into GW on an acronym. Both of GW's akas are held UNLINKABLE (aka_unlinkable) for exactly that reason — the ledger carries at least four GWFs and the served corpus mentions at least three that are not this one.

review_queue.name: RSPWF wing — three rulings recorded, not decided (newsgroup-as-wing / hub house_style / Usenet-corpus lot)
review_queue.note: RSPWF wing handoff §6–7 (2026-08-23), batched for the Janitor rather than filed as three separate entries. (1) THE NEWSGROUP-VS-SITE QUESTION: rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy predates RSPWF.com, outlived it, and is where the community actually was; this accession recorded the relationship three ways (a `Serves:` placard row, the epitaph's own first paragraph, the `medium_detail` string) and wrote no `affiliations.json` edge — an edge needs a row on the other end, and a newsgroup is not a promotion. The hub-entity gavel makes a community INSTITUTION holdable; a Usenet newsgroup is a community institution with no site, no owner and no closing date, and this is the first time the museum has held something that plainly serves one. Two honest readings, undecided: the newsgroup stays context, named in prose and never a row (the conservative reading this lane took); or `medium: usenet` (already in the vocabulary) covers it and rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy should have a wing of its own, with rspwf.com as an affiliated hub. (2) THE HUB house_style GAP: the prose-by-tier doctrine says a Tier 2 promotion owes a `house_style`; `house_style` is defined as how a fed staged its own booking, and a hub books nothing. The field is left absent on RSPWF's own promotions.json row, the soft warning stands deliberately, and the fix is either a hub clause in the ladder or a widened definition (“how the institution conducted itself”) — first real cost of the hub-entity gavel. (3) THE USENET-CORPUS LOT: two of the 12,175 rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy messages in the workshop's Usenet corpus are served in this wing and were folded into lot 0042 rather than given a lot of their own. A lot covering that corpus is a real decision — it would be retro-applied to anything else already drawing on it — and it is bigger than this one wing.

The other three ledger ICWs split the same way: a bare PCW résumé mention with no date, a fantasywrestling.com member of 1999, and MWE's own Illinois Championship Wrestling development territory of 2009. review_queue.name: A tribute show staged on PWE Inc.'s own board for one of its own members, late 2005
review_queue.note: FLAGGED, NOT ACTED ON. The board's own 2005 forum tree carries an inter-promotional forum whose description reads “Come here to RP and take part in the special tribute show for PWE's very own <name>”, and its own Announcements forum carries threads titled “Tributes?”, “Last Call — to sign up to RP at <first name>'s Tribute show” and “PWE DEAD — omg!!!”, all in November 2005; two characters' own career ledgers list matches worked at that show. Seven months earlier the same member had opened a thread of his own titled “Not a thread I'm thrilled to make..... — But it's time people knew.” No statement of a death survives anywhere in the corpus, so the memorial verification bar is NOT cleared on this evidence and no memorial is proposed: the name would need out-of-fiction corroboration, and the museum grants a memorial only by gavel. The name and every receipt are in a workshop file; the repository carries none of them. The same name was redacted this pass from a served year-end awards ballot under the real-name rule — one edit to reverse if the memorial is ever granted, since a memorial name is never redacted. Filed by the PWE-board siblings accession (2026-08-24). PROBE CONCLUDED (coordinator, 2026-08-24): the Wayback Machine's complete census for this board is 201 captures, and none of the five key URLs — the member's own April 2005 disclosure thread (topic 7829), the three November announcement threads (10828, 10897, 10918), or the tribute forum itself (showforum=150) — was ever archived; their contents are unrecoverable from the Archive (a control query against a known-held topic verified the method). External public records show no matching death in the window (the sole 2005 obituary for the name is January — timeline-incompatible with the member's own April post). STANDING RECOMMENDATION pending further evidence: the record supports 'the community held a tribute show for this member' and nothing more — a tribute of unverified nature; the v74 redaction stands, no memorial is claimed, the December 2005 board index stays unserved. Community testimony through the Janitor's own channels remains the one open avenue. GAVELED (the Janitor, 2026-08-24): the name remains a hunt target for further information but is NOT memorialized unless and until he is encountered again — not to gatekeep the honor, but because he may have survived and lived a long and fruitful life, and memorializing a living person would violate the privacy prohibition itself. The Janitor will pursue further OSINT personally. The v74 redaction stands; the December 2005 board index stays unserved.

review_queue.note: CURATION.md v78 was applied to FAW's 2001 corpus and the worked example was carried only as far as its two deepest-receipted cases: lex-luger-faw and british-bulldog-faw are minted on staged activity per v78(a), and the three faw-universal reigns that carried them as unminted holders now resolve to real entities. The corpus carries far more than two. review_queue.name: "Diamond Girl" Heidi Leick — GDWA's own vs. the RSPWF Top 200's own ranked wrestler
review_queue.note: THE STRONGEST OF THE THREE GDWA JOIN HITS, and the one closest to a verdict. Four separate signals line up and none of them has been treated as a merge. (1) NAME PLUS MONIKER, exactly: GDWA's own card of 18 January 2000 bills "'Diamond Girl' Heidi Leick" (promotions/gdwa/archive/scratching-post-2000-02-28.html); the ranked entity's own aka is "\"Diamond Girl\" Heidi Leick". (2) ERA: the ranked placings are 1998 #136 and 1999 #44, immediately before GDWA's own January 2000 card. (3) FEDERATION: the 1999 tag is IEWA, and GDWA's own home page links the IEWA by full name as "International Electronic Wrestling Association... A great new fed with a Women's Division" — the two women's-division feds of the same moment, one linking the other. (4) WORKSHOP CORROBORATION, not served and not a museum holding: the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy thread index carries a posting of 28 December 1999 titled "[GDWA] Heidi Leick -Flash-", and a 2002 post in a workshop file carries a signature claiming both of the exact placings the ranked entity's own row records. The name-plus-moniker doctrine is explicit that this is stronger evidence than a bare name and still never sufficient on its own, so nothing here is merged: this entry is filed for a human verdict, and it is ready for one. (5) A FIFTH SIGNAL, added by the newsgroup-deepening pass of 2026-08-24 and still not a merge: the handler is the same person on both sides. A post of 31 December 2003 in a workshop file, subject "GDWA- to all the former Women...", opens "Hey all, Frankie Starz here * Handles Heidi Leick *" — and Frankie Starz is the handle GDWA's own site credits for building it ("G.D.W.A.'s own Frankie Starz put up this site"), while the same handler's newsgroup signature is the one carrying both of the exact placings the ranked entity's own row records. So GDWA's Heidi Leick and the RSPWF-ranked "Diamond Girl" Heidi Leick share a name, a moniker, an era, a linked federation AND a handler. This is now as strong as a name collision gets short of a fed document saying so, and it is STILL not merged here: the merge is a human verdict and this pass had no mandate to take it. Ready for one, more so than before. SEPARATELY SETTLED, so it is not re-litigated inside this question: the NAMESAKE. The character is named for the actress Hudson Leick (Callisto in Xena: Warrior Princess), born Heidi Hudson Leick — recorded 2026-08-24 as a "Named for" edge, heidi-leick-gdwa portrays hudson-leick in data/external-figures.json. That is an etymology and explicitly NOT a v78 portrayal: Hudson Leick is an actress, not a wrestler, GDWA barred real wrestlers from its roster outright, and the character is the fed's own original. The namesake edge says nothing either way about whether these two rows are one character.
review_queue.resolution_note: Resolved in the v104 contagion sweep (2026-08-30): merged at presumed grade on the standing rule (see the v104 erratum), as a Fejona-class convergence — the five signals this entry's own note already laid out (name plus moniker, adjacent era, GDWA's own IEWA link matching the ranked tag, the workshop newsgroup corroboration, and the shared Frankie Starz handler) taken together clear the merge bar without an explicit document. heidi-leick-gdwa survives; the-diamond-girl-heidi-leick-rspwf is retired and its RSPWF Top 200 bestowals repoint here. review_queue.name: The PRODIGY diaspora: 19 CSWA mints against their same-named NFW/UWA/AAWC rows
review_queue.note: The CSWA accession (lot 0062) mints its whole roster under -cswa-qualified slugs, and nineteen of those names are already registered in this museum off NFW, UWA and AAWC — the PRODIGY-descended federations the CSWA's own people went on to. The evidence for one character per pair is real and it is not a bare name match: the CSWA roster reappears in those feds TOGETHER rather than one name at a time, NFW's own retrospective About page names the CSWA alongside the UWA and the fWo as fellow PRODIGY leagues, NFW holds the CSWA's own ULTRATITLE under a stated leasing agreement, and the CSWA's own board threads on fwrestling.com run alongside NFW's on the same board in the same years. What is missing is an explicit statement: no document held here says of any pair that they are the same character. Per the no-auto-merge-and-no-silent-distinctness rule the accession registered them separately and recorded the collision on each new row's own identity[] entry rather than merging. A merge would rewrite rows in the nfw/uwa/aawc shards, which the CSWA lane does not write. Held for a coordinator verdict, pair by pair or as a set. The pairs: aaron-douglas-cswa / aaron-douglas; alex-wylde-cswa / alex-wylde; cameron-cruise / cameron-cruise; deacon / deacon; eddy-love / eddy-love; eli-flair / eli-flair; evan-aho / evan-aho; flic-rair / flic-rair; guns-aawc / guns-aawc; hornet / hornet; joey-melton / joey-melton; kevin-powers / kevin-powers; lawrence-stanley / lawrence-stanley; mark-windham / mark-windham; mark-windsor / mark-windsor; mike-randalls / mike-randalls; steve-radder / steve-radder; tom-adler / tom-adler; troy-windham-cswa / troy-windham.
review_queue.resolution_note: The Janitor's own set verdict (2026-08-26, verbatim: "Yes, those characters should be linked across those promotions"), clarified the same day to a true merge ("Aren't we just merging the characters that were obviously the same across multiple promotions?"): all nineteen pairs collapsed into their pre-existing NFW/AAWC canonical rows. Each -cswa row's tenure was folded onto the canonical row's tenures[] verbatim (grade/source/notes preserved), aka/notes/portrays facts folded in where they added (three CSWA-billed nicknames — "Hurricane" Eddy Love, "Good God" Kevin Powers, "Iceman" Steve Radder — became aka entries; hornet's Sting portrayal note and mark-windham's Barry Windham portrayal note carried over; hornet's and deacon's own CSWA notes folded in), each canonical row's notes[] gained a one-line merge record citing the ruling and the pair's own receipt (a pre-existing nfw+uwa or nfw+uwa+aawc multi-tenure shape for hornet, joey-melton, mike-randalls, tom-adler, alex-wylde and troy-windham; the population-level receipt — whole rosters overlapping together, NFW's own About page naming the CSWA a fellow PRODIGY league, NFW leasing the CSWA's own Ultratitle, shared fwrestling.com/NFW board years — for the rest). 35 championship-reign holder ids repointed from the retired -cswa ids to their canonical ids in data/shards/cswa/reigns.json (a full sweep of shows/rps/units across every shard found no other reference anywhere in the registry). All nineteen -cswa rows were deleted from data/shards/cswa/characters.json and data/aliases.json now redirects each retired id to its canonical id. `guns-cswa` merged into `guns-aawc` (the AAWC row, per the coordinator's canonical-selection rule favoring the older/richer pre-existing row). One pair the set evidence would otherwise have swept in — tsunami-cswa against NFW's akita-nfw (Tsunami is one of Akita's own akas) — was NOT merged: it already carries its own reasoned, receipted `distinct` identity assertion (different primary name, different decade, different billed nationality — a 1995 twenty-year-old Unified World Champion versus a 2008–2013 Japan-billed Brawl-show wrestler), the digest itself resolved it distinct on that specific evidence rather than on generic-name caution alone, and forcing a flip here would override a evidence-based call with none of its own — flagged to the coordinator rather than forced, per the standing stop-on-contradiction rule. See a workshop file for the full per-pair ledger. UPDATE (2026-09-02): a SECOND wave of the same collision was found by the AAWC tier-3 pass — nineteen more CSWA rows minted against this wing's after the verdict landed. Fourteen were merged on per-pair primary-source receipts and five held; see the "PRODIGY diaspora, wave two" entry below and a workshop file.

review_queue.name: HBK 2000 / HBK2000 (CSWA) — one competitor under two spellings, filed as two rows
review_queue.note: Proposed merge at primary-source grade, receipted inside one served document. The Greensboro Championship Tournament bracket (/promotions/cswa/archive/greensboro-championship-tournament-the-bracket-1998-08.html, source http://fwrestling.com/archives/1998/gboro.htm) lists Group B as exactly four competitors — R. Jaminson, Nemesis, HBK 2000, Mysterious — and spells the same competitor both ways across its own schedule: 'Mysterious def. HBK2000' at PRIMETIME in Vancouver, 'HBK 2000 def. Randall Jaminson' at PRIMETIME in Seattle, 'Nemesis def. HBK2000' at PRIMETIME in Baltimore. The group's own arithmetic closes on four men, not five: the standings table gives that competitor a 1-2 record worth three points, which is exactly the three matches a four-man round robin gives each entrant, and the two spellings supply those three results between them with no overlap and no fourth man. The federation's own table therefore treats the two spellings as one competitor. The held rows split on an axis the document does not: hbk2000-cswa carries a 1998-only CSWA tenure and is the id the Vancouver card's structured side uses, while hbk-2000-cswa carries a 1998-1999 tenure and is the id the Seattle and Baltimore cards use. No served document stages two HBKs, on the same night or against each other. Held here rather than applied, per the no-auto-merge discipline. If merged, hbk-2000-cswa carries the fuller record and is the natural surviving id, with the retired id carried forward in aliases.json and the Vancouver card's structured side repointed.

review_queue.name: CSWA Greensboro Championship, August 1998 – January 1999: a tournament to crown a champion runs across a recorded reign
review_queue.note: Both readings recorded; nothing changed. The served bracket document (/promotions/cswa/archive/greensboro-championship-tournament-the-bracket-1998-08.html, source http://fwrestling.com/archives/1998/gboro.htm) states in its own voice that 'the latest Greensboro Tournament began in August 1998 and continued until ELVIS LIVES XI on January 24, 1999', and its final line is 'Aaron Douglas defeats Apocalypse' — four groups of round robin into a single-elimination final, the shape a federation uses to fill a title rather than to produce a challenger. The held reign rows read the same months differently: cswa-greensboro-r007 has blade-cswa holding the belt from 1999 at year precision, with no event wired, until 1999-01-24, and cswa-greensboro-r004 then has Aaron Douglas winning it on 1999-01-24 at ELVIS LIVES XI. The outcome and the date agree; whether the belt was vacant while the tournament ran does not. Two further facts sit between them: SuperPRIMETIME in Charleston (http://fwrestling.com/archives/1998/spt1210.htm) has Blade debuting on 10 December 1998, four months into the tournament, so a Blade reign inside that window is chronologically possible and the bracket simply never mentions him; and the bracket never says the title was vacant. The 1999 cards the reign chain turns on are served but their sources sit outside the 1988/1990/1995/1998 directories.

review_queue.name: Louis Bourbon (thReat) vs Louis Bourbon (UWF)
review_queue.resolution_note: Merged, graded primary-source, after the Janitor's D97 ruling of 27 September 2026 (keep separate, defer to primary-source evidence in our holdings). The UWF's own texts supply it: Seth Silver's promo of 9 October 2005 (“This is a proud Frenchman … a company felt it necessary to make him portray a delusional heir to the Bourbon monarchy”) describes the thReat gimmick from the other side, the same promo's “Rebecca” is Sean's Laura Whittle by the fed's own commentary of 26 October 2005, and the Live and Loud 5 credits name Sean among the writers of “The Uprising -v- Chris Storm”.
